board: TGA Islamic Studies scheme (aqeedah, fiqh, seerah, hadith, akhlaq)
source: Adapted from TGA Drive RE/Islamic Studies folder (Al-Baseerah Salah quiz KS2: salah, nafs, sincerity; Edexcel International GCSE Islamic Studies SOW, Theme 1 (life of the Prophet ﷺ) to shape the seerah sequence); National Curriculum RE (KS2) | Spring 1 2027 (lessons 1, 4, 5, 6 upgraded, 13 new): Year 4 pack Islamic Studies Spring 1 (weeks 1 and 2 Autumn bridge: Islam, Iman, Ihsan and the six articles; weeks 3 to 5 the Makkan years condensed); hadith of Jibril (Muslim 8), the first revelation (Bukhari 3) and Mount Safa (Bukhari, Book of Tafsir) described; reliable children's seerah TO CONFIRM | Spring 2 2027 (lessons 14 to 19 new): Year 4 pack Islamic Studies Spring 2 weeks 1 to 6 (Bilal and Sumayyah; Abyssinia; Umar; the boycott; the Year of Sorrow; Isra and Mi'raj); seerah reports labelled; 2:153, 16:90, 41:44, 94:5-6, 2:155, 17:1; hadith from Bukhari and Muslim; lessons v3

lessons.title: Bridge: Islam, Iman and Ihsan (the hadith of Jibril)
lessons.bigQuestion: Would you do your homework differently if you knew someone important was watching? Why?
objectives: To understand the three levels of the religion taught in the hadith of Jibril: Islam, Iman and Ihsan
successCriteria: All: retell the hadith of Jibril in four steps
Most: define Islam, Iman and Ihsan
Some: give an everyday example of ihsan
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: excellence and sincerity in worship

keywords.def: submitting to Allah through the five pillars
belief in the heart in the six articles
worshipping Allah as though you see Him
the angel who brings Allah's revelation

hook.text: Would you do your homework differently if you knew someone important was watching? Why?
hook.a: Yes. Ihsan is remembering Allah always sees us, so we always do our best.

islamicLink.text: The hadith of Jibril (Muslim 8): the Prophet ﷺ explained Islam, Iman and Ihsan, then said Jibril had come to teach the people their religion.

starter.q: How many pillars of Islam are there?
How many articles of iman are there?
Name the pillar that is fasting.
Which city was the Prophet ﷺ born in?

teach.heading: A visitor in white
bullets: A man with very white clothes
Very black hair, no sign of travel
He sat knee to knee with the Prophet ﷺ
teach.note: Retell the hadith of Jibril from Umar (Muslim 8) in your own words. Nobody knew the visitor. No picture of the angel is ever shown.

teach.heading: Three questions
teach.note: Pupils copy the table into their books.

head: He asked about
The answer in short
rows: Belief in Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, qadar
Worship Allah as if you see Him; He sees you

teach.heading: Who was the visitor?
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ said: it was Jibril
He came to teach you your religion
teach.note: Point out the adab of learning: Jibril sat close, asked clearly, listened. Link to how we behave in class.

options: Worshipping Allah as if you see Him
check.why: Fasting is a pillar of Islam and angels are part of iman. Ihsan is the highest level: excellence.

practice.q: Define Islam, Iman and Ihsan in one line each.
practice.a: Islam: the five pillars. Iman: belief in the six articles. Ihsan: worshipping Allah as if you see Him.
practice.model: Islam is what I do: the five pillars. Iman is what I believe: six articles. Ihsan is how well I do it: as if I see Allah.

practice.q: Who was the visitor in the hadith?
practice.a: Jibril

practice.q: Give one example of ihsan in prayer.
practice.a: For example: praying slowly and calmly, not rushing.

independent.q: Draw three steps labelled Islam, Iman, Ihsan, with one example for each.
independent.a: Islam: praying five times. Iman: believing in angels. Ihsan: praying with full focus.
independent.model: Teacher draws the bottom step, labels it Islam, and writes 'I pray Fajr'.

independent.q: Extend: how did Jibril show good manners of learning?
independent.a: He sat close, asked clearly and listened.

independent.q: Stretch: why is ihsan the highest level?
independent.a: It needs Islam and iman, and doing them with the best effort and sincerity.

exit.q: Believing in the six articles is called ...
Back to our ponder: how does ihsan change the way we work?
exit.a: We do our best because Allah always sees us.

lessons.homework: Do one task at home with ihsan (your very best, even if no one checks) and write what you did.
lessons.send: SEND: three-step picture card. EAL: word bank with meanings. Stretch: write how ihsan applies to being kind to others.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Aqeedah: Islam, Iman and Ihsan
lessons.title: Believing in Allah's names and attributes
objectives: Explain that Allah's names and attributes are in the Qur'an and Sunnah
Explain the way of the Salaf: affirm without comparing or denying
Give examples of names and attributes

keywords.def: a quality of Allah, like hearing or seeing
accept as true what Allah says about Himself
those who follow the Prophet's ﷺ way and the Companions

teach.heading: Names and attributes
bullets: Allah has the most beautiful names
We call upon Him by them
teach.note: Bismillah. Qur'an 7:180. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah has ninety-nine names and whoever memorises/learns and acts on them enters Jannah (Bukhari and Muslim). Explain the number does not limit His names.

teach.heading: Nothing is like Him
teach.note: Qur'an 42:11. Explain: Allah's attributes are real but not like ours. We do not compare Allah to creation (tashbih). Our hearing is not like His.

teach.heading: The way of the Salaf
bullets: We affirm what Allah said about Himself
We affirm what the Prophet ﷺ said
teach.note: Ahl as-sunnah follow the Companions: believe in the names and attributes as they came, without denial, distortion, asking how, or comparing. Keep it clear and concise. Do not quote unverified statements of scholars.

teach.heading: Examples
teach.note: Qur'an 20:5: the Most Merciful rose above the Throne in a manner that suits His majesty. Say we believe it as it came, without asking how. This is enough for Year 4.

teach.heading: Why learn them?
teach.note: Qur'an 7:180 links names to dua. Give an example: call Ar-Razzaq when asking for provision, Al-Ghafur when asking for forgiveness. Pairs make a dua with names.

independent: Match names with meanings: Al-Ghafur / Ar-Razzaq / Al-Basir / As-Sami'
Write a dua using two names
Explain 42:11 in your own words
exit: What does 'there is nothing like Him' teach?
Why do we not ask 'how' about Allah's attributes?
lessons.homework: Learn five more names of Allah with meanings and share them at home.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: name cards with meanings and pictures. Stretch: explain the difference between affirming and comparing.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Aqeedah: Islam, Iman and Ihsan
lessons.title: Belief in the messengers: the seal of the prophets
objectives: Explain why Allah sent messengers
Name some messengers and their message
Explain that Muhammad ﷺ is the last prophet

keywords.def: one sent by Allah with a message

starter: Name the book given to Musa.

teach.heading: Why messengers?
bullets: Allah did not leave us without guidance
To call to worship Allah alone
teach.note: Bismillah. Qur'an 16:36: We sent into every nation a messenger saying worship Allah and avoid false gods. Ask: why do we need guidance?

teach.heading: Some messengers
teach.note: Mention that Allah named 25 prophets in the Qur'an and many others were sent. Link to earlier stories. Misconception: Muslims believe Isa was God's son; clarify Isa was a mighty messenger and servant of Allah (4:171).

teach.heading: The last prophet
bullets: Muhammad ﷺ is the seal of the prophets
teach.note: Qur'an 33:40. Explain his message is for all people and is preserved. The Prophet ﷺ said there will be no prophet after him (Bukhari and Muslim). Relate to why the Qur'an is final.

teach.heading: Our duty to the Prophet ﷺ
teach.note: Qur'an 3:31: if you love Allah, follow me, Allah will love you. Ask: how do we show love? Follow his Sunnah. Avoid innovations: we love him by following, not by adding to religion.

teach.heading: Respect all prophets
bullets: We do not differentiate between them
teach.note: Qur'an 2:285: we make no distinction between any of His messengers. Teach the sayings. Quiz on prophets.

practice: Name the seal of the prophets.
independent: Match the prophet to the book: Musa / Dawud / Isa / Muhammad ﷺ
Write why the last prophet's message is for everyone
Make a timeline of five prophets
exit: What does 'seal of the prophets' mean?
Name two prophets and their message.
lessons.homework: Find out one new thing about a prophet from the Qur'an and share it.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: prophet cards with pictures of symbols (no faces). Stretch: explain the importance of following the Sunnah.

lessons.title: Arabia before Islam, the birth and childhood of the Prophet ﷺ
lessons.bigQuestion: What do you think it would be like to grow up without your parents? Who would you need?
objectives: To understand what Makkah was like before Islam and how Allah cared for the Prophet ﷺ as an orphan
successCriteria: All: describe Makkah before Islam in three facts
Most: order four events of his early childhood
Some: explain how Allah cared for him

keywords.def: the city of the Ka'bah where the Prophet ﷺ was born
a child whose parent has died
the year an army with elephants tried to destroy the Ka'bah

hook.text: What do you think it would be like to grow up without your parents? Who would you need?
hook.a: Loving family and Allah's care. The Prophet ﷺ had both.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?' (ad-Duha 93:6).

starter.q: How many articles of iman are there?
Who was the visitor in the hadith of Jibril?
What is ihsan?
starter.a: Worshipping Allah as if you see Him

starter.q: Which book came to Musa?

teach.heading: Makkah before Islam
bullets: The Ka'bah was full of idols
Some girls were wronged; the weak were not protected
teach.note: Describe it simply: the house Ibrahim built for Allah alone was filled with idols. Allah mentions the Quraysh trade journeys in winter and summer (Quraysh 106:1-2).

teach.heading: The Year of the Elephant
bullets: An army with an elephant came
They wanted to destroy the Ka'bah
teach.note: Surah al-Fil (105) tells the story. The Prophet ﷺ was born in this same year, in Makkah. No pictures of the Prophet ﷺ.

teach.heading: A childhood in Allah's care
teach.note: Build the timeline strip with the class.

timeline.label: Baby
timeline.text: Cared for by Halimah in the desert

timeline.label: Age 8
timeline.text: Grandfather Abd al-Muttalib died; uncle Abu Talib cared for him

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: Who looked after him from the age of eight?
check.why: His mother died when he was six; Halimah cared for him as a baby; Abu Talib from age eight.

practice.q: Order: Abu Talib, Halimah, Abd al-Muttalib, Aminah dies.
practice.a: Halimah, Aminah dies, Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Talib
practice.model: As a baby: Halimah. At six: his mother Aminah died. Then grandfather Abd al-Muttalib. At eight: Abu Talib.

practice.q: Which surah tells the story of the elephant?
practice.a: Surah al-Fil

practice.q: Give one fact about Makkah before Islam.
practice.a: For example: the Ka'bah was full of idols.

independent.q: Add four events to your seerah timeline strip, each with a short caption.
independent.a: Birth in the Year of the Elephant; Halimah; mother dies at 6; Abu Talib from 8.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first box: 'Year of the Elephant: born in Makkah.'

independent.q: Extend: how did Allah care for the young orphan?
independent.a: He gave him loving carers: Halimah, his grandfather and his uncle.

independent.q: Stretch: Allah asks, 'Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?' (ad-Duha 93:6). What does this teach us about orphans?
independent.a: Allah cares for orphans, so we must care for them too.

exit.q: The Prophet ﷺ was born in ...
Back to our ponder: who did he need, and who did Allah give him?
exit.a: Loving carers: Halimah, his grandfather and his uncle Abu Talib.

lessons.homework: Tell your family the story of the Year of the Elephant from Surah al-Fil in your own words.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards for the four carers. EAL: timeline word bank. Stretch: explain why the Ka'bah mattered to Quraysh.

lessons.title: The honest trader, Khadijah and the Cave of Hira
lessons.bigQuestion: What makes you trust someone? Can trust be bought?
objectives: To understand how the Prophet's ﷺ honesty earned trust and how the first revelation came in the Cave of Hira
successCriteria: All: explain why he was called al-Amin
Most: describe his work for Khadijah
Some: retell the first revelation and the first words revealed
lessons.smsc: Moral: honesty in work and trade

keywords.def: a respected businesswoman who became his wife
a cave on a mountain near Makkah
revelation: Allah's message to a prophet

hook.text: What makes you trust someone? Can trust be bought?
hook.a: Honesty over a long time. It cannot be bought: it is earned.

islamicLink.text: Allah describes the Prophet ﷺ: 'And indeed, you are of a great moral character' (al-Qalam 68:4).

starter.q: Who cared for the Prophet ﷺ from age eight?
Which surah tells of the elephant army?
In which city was he born?
What does orphan mean?
starter.a: A child whose parent has died

teach.heading: Al-Amin
teach.note: Explain that Quraysh called him al-Amin long before prophethood. He also shepherded sheep as a young man (Bukhari).

teach.heading: Trading for Khadijah
bullets: He was honest and made good profit
She admired his character; they married
teach.note: Commonly reported in the seerah: he led her caravan to Syria and was honest in every deal. Their marriage was full of love and respect.

teach.heading: The Cave of Hira
bullets: He went to Hira to think and worship
'Read in the name of your Lord'
teach.note: Retell from Bukhari 3 simply: Jibril said Iqra; the Prophet ﷺ said he could not read; then the first ayat (al-Alaq 96:1-5) were revealed. He returned home shaking.

quote.text: Read in the name of your Lord who created. Created man from a clinging substance. Read, and your Lord is the most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man that which he knew not.

teach.heading: Khadijah comforts him
bullets: She covered him and calmed him
She said Allah would never disgrace him
Because he was kind and helped others
teach.note: Bukhari 3 reports she listed his good deeds: keeping ties with family, helping the weak, honouring guests.

check.q: What was the first word revealed?
check.why: Jibril said 'Iqra' in the Cave of Hira (al-Alaq 96:1).

practice.q: Why was he called al-Amin?
practice.a: Because he was always honest and trustworthy
practice.model: People left their valuables with him. He never lied or cheated. So they named him al-Amin: the trustworthy.

practice.q: Where did the first revelation come?
practice.a: The Cave of Hira

practice.q: How old was he at the first revelation?
practice.a: Forty

independent.q: Add the trader years, marriage and Hira to your timeline strip with captions.
independent.a: Trader for Khadijah; married Khadijah; age 40: first revelation in Hira.

independent.q: Extend: list two good deeds Khadijah reminded him of.
independent.a: He kept ties with family and helped the weak.

independent.q: Stretch: why did his honesty help people believe him later?
independent.a: They knew he had never lied, so they had reason to trust his message.

exit.q: Al-Amin means ...
Back to our ponder: how did the Prophet ﷺ earn trust?
exit.a: By always being honest, over many years.

lessons.homework: Learn al-Alaq 96:1-5 with its meaning and recite it to your family.
lessons.send: SEND: picture timeline cards. EAL: key word cards with Arabic. Stretch: explain why the first word was about reading and learning.

lessons.title: The first Muslims and the public call
lessons.bigQuestion: If everyone laughed at you for telling the truth, would you keep telling it?
objectives: To understand who the first Muslims were and how the call to Islam became public
successCriteria: All: name four of the first Muslims
Most: retell the call from Mount Safa
Some: explain why patience was needed
lessons.smsc: Moral: courage to tell the truth with patience

keywords.def: staying calm and keeping going through hardship

hook.text: If everyone laughed at you for telling the truth, would you keep telling it?
hook.a: The first Muslims did, with patience and trust in Allah.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And warn your closest kindred' (ash-Shu'ara 26:214).

starter.q: What was the first word revealed?
Where did the first revelation come?
What does al-Amin mean?
Who comforted him after Hira?

teach.heading: The first believers
teach.note: Point out the variety: a woman, a friend, a boy, a freed servant.

head: First Muslim
Who they were
rows: His wife: the first to believe
Freed servant, raised in his home

teach.heading: Quiet then public
bullets: About three years of quiet da'wah
teach.note: Allah revealed 'And warn your closest kindred' (ash-Shu'ara 26:214). Bukhari reports the event on Safa.

teach.heading: On Mount Safa
bullets: 'We have never known you to lie'
He warned them about worshipping idols
teach.note: Retell: he asked if they would believe him if he warned of an army behind the hill; they said they had never known him lie. Abu Lahab rejected him; Surah al-Masad was revealed.

check.q: What did the people on Safa say about him?
options: They had never known him to lie
check.why: They admitted his honesty, even those who then rejected his message.

teach.heading: Patience
bullets: Many in Quraysh mocked the Muslims
teach.note: Link to sabr. Keep stories gentle for Year 4; persecution is taught in more detail later.

practice.q: Name the first woman, man, boy and freed servant to believe.
practice.a: Khadijah, Abu Bakr, Ali, Zayd ibn Harithah
practice.model: First woman: Khadijah. First man (friend): Abu Bakr. First boy: Ali. First freed servant: Zayd.

practice.q: Which ayah told him to warn his family?
Why did people on Safa trust his words?
practice.a: They had never known him to lie.

independent.q: Write a short news report: 'The call from Mount Safa'. Use who, where, what, how people reacted.
independent.a: Who: the Prophet ﷺ; where: Mount Safa; what: he warned them to worship Allah alone; reaction: some agreed he was honest, Abu Lahab rejected.
independent.model: Teacher writes the headline and first line: 'Makkah: Today Muhammad ﷺ climbed Mount Safa and called the tribes.'

independent.q: Extend: add the public call to your timeline strip.
independent.a: About age 43: public call from Mount Safa.

independent.q: Stretch: why do you think the call began quietly?
independent.a: To build a strong group of believers first and protect them.

exit.q: The first person to believe was ...
Back to our ponder: what kept the first Muslims going?

lessons.homework: Ask your family to name the first four Muslims, then teach them any they missed.
lessons.send: SEND: four name cards with pictures of places (no people). EAL: report frame with headings. Stretch: explain the lesson of Surah al-Masad.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh: purity, the pillars of salah and congregation
lessons.title: Purity: wudu, ghusl and tayammum
objectives: Explain minor and major impurity
Know ghusl and tayammum
Give examples of when each applies

keywords.def: purification with clean earth when water is not available

starter: Name the obligatory parts of wudu.

teach.heading: Two types
teach.note: Bismillah. Qur'an 5:6 also mentions purifying oneself for major impurity. Explain at an age-appropriate level. Older children will cover details in later years. Use clear, matter-of-fact language.

teach.heading: Ghusl
bullets: Intend and wash the whole body
teach.note: Keep it light: ghusl is a full wash required after specific occasions that children will learn about as they grow. Do not go into private details. Mention Friday ghusl is recommended (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: Tayammum
bullets: Used when there is no water or it harms
teach.note: Qur'an 5:6 (and 4:43). Tayammum: intention, strike the earth once, wipe the face and then hands. Different schools vary slightly; teach the basic. Demonstrate.

teach.heading: Clean surroundings
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ taught cleanliness. Use the example of being careful to keep prayer clothes clean. Do not give contested rulings.

teach.heading: Practice
teach.note: Scenario cards with simple examples (no water on a journey, breaking wudu). Keep to non-sensitive cases.

independent: Draw a flowchart: how do I purify?
Write three differences between wudu and ghusl
Explain tayammum in 5 steps
exit: Name the two kinds of impurity.
lessons.homework: Ask a parent how to keep clothes pure for prayer and write notes.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: flowchart with pictures. Stretch: research why Islam provides tayammum.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh: purity, the pillars of salah and congregation
lessons.title: Salah: conditions and pillars
objectives: List the conditions of salah
List the pillars (arkan) of salah
Explain the difference

keywords.def: a part inside the prayer you cannot leave out

teach.heading: Conditions
bullets: Facing Qiblah, time, covering the awrah
teach.note: Bismillah. These come before the prayer. Facing the Qiblah: Qur'an 2:144. Time: 4:103. Covering: pupils will learn details in later years. Keep gentle.

teach.heading: Pillars
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said there is no prayer for one who does not recite Fatihah (Bukhari and Muslim). Different madhhabs list pillars in slightly different ways; present the common ones.

teach.heading: Sujood and sitting
teach.note: Sujood: the closest a servant is to Allah (Muslim). Tasleem: salam to right and left. Demonstrate.

teach.heading: Calmness
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ told the man: pray again, you did not pray
teach.note: Bukhari and Muslim (Abu Hurairah): the man who prayed hastily. The Prophet ﷺ taught him to be calm in each position. Ask: why is calmness important?

teach.heading: Practise
teach.note: Matching game. Keep to the core. Praise accuracy.

independent: Sort cards: condition vs pillar
Write the order of one rak'ah
Role-play teaching salah
exit: What is a pillar of salah?
lessons.homework: Pray one salah calmly and write a short reflection on how it felt.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: card sort with pictures. Stretch: explain the difference between a pillar and a sunnah.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Fiqh: purity, the pillars of salah and congregation
lessons.title: Congregational prayer and Jumuah
objectives: Explain the reward of praying in congregation
Describe Jumuah etiquette
Explain the khutbah

teach.heading: The reward
teach.note: Bismillah. The Prophet ﷺ said prayer in congregation is 27 degrees better than praying alone. Explain 'degrees' as multiples of reward. Link to community.

teach.heading: Straight lines
teach.note: Straight lines: Bukhari and Muslim. Do not rush ahead of the imam. Practice on screen.

teach.heading: Jumuah
teach.note: Qur'an 62:9: when the call is made for Friday prayer, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. Obligatory for men; ladies may attend. Teach the Friday sunnahs: ghusl, clean clothes, going early (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: Listening to the khutbah
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said if you say 'be quiet' to your friend while the imam speaks, you have spoken idly (Bukhari and Muslim). Use gently.

teach.heading: Masjid manners
bullets: Pray two rak'ahs on entering (tahiyyat al-masjid)
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said when one of you enters the masjid, do not sit until praying two rak'ahs (Bukhari and Muslim). Role-play enters the masjid.

independent: Plan a Jumuah morning routine
Explain three Friday etiquettes
Write a paragraph about unity in prayer
exit: How much more reward is congregational prayer?
What do we do when the imam speaks?
lessons.homework: Attend a Jumuah or watch one online and write three things you noticed.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: pictures of lines in the masjid. Stretch: explain why straight lines matter.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Akhlaq and hadith: trust, family and neighbours
lessons.title: Truthfulness and trustworthiness
objectives: Explain the hadith of truthfulness
Explain amanah
Apply truthfulness and trust in school

teach.heading: The hadith
bullets: Lying leads to wrongdoing and the Fire
teach.note: Bismillah. Bukhari and Muslim (Ibn Mas'ud). Read the full hadith. A person keeps telling the truth until recorded with Allah as truthful. Ask: how might this change a life?

teach.heading: Amanah
bullets: Keep secrets that should be kept
teach.note: Qur'an 4:58: Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due. Relate to school, borrowing a book. Ask for examples.

teach.heading: Signs of hypocrisy
teach.note: Bukhari and Muslim: the signs of the hypocrite are three. Use carefully; it is a warning and an encouragement to improve. Do not label peers.

teach.heading: Restore trust
teach.note: Scenario: you lost a friend's book. What do you do? Role-play. Praise honesty.

teach.heading: Trust poster
teach.note: Pairs make a poster 'Be a person of amanah'. Display.

independent: Write a scenario about trust and explain the best choice
Explain the hadith in a paragraph
Create a rules chart for being trustworthy
lessons.homework: Return or fix something borrowed this week and tell us what you learned.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with sentence frames. Stretch: link the hadith to Al-Amin.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Akhlaq and hadith: trust, family and neighbours
lessons.title: Honouring parents and family
objectives: Explain Allah's command to honour parents
Explain the hadith about the mother
Describe ways to show respect
starter: Who does Allah tell us to be good to?

teach.heading: Command in the Qur'an
bullets: Worship Allah alone and be good to parents
teach.note: Bismillah. Qur'an 17:23-24: your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him and be good to parents; if one or both reach old age do not say 'uff' or scold. Speak a noble word. Explain 'uff' as the smallest sign of impatience.

teach.heading: Mercy
bullets: as they raised me when I was small
teach.note: 17:24. Teach the dua: Rabbir hamhuma kama rabbayani saghira. Link to Reception where children first heard it. Ask what parents do for us.

teach.heading: Who deserves my company most?
bullets: A man asked: who is most deserving?
Prophet ﷺ: your mother, your mother, your mother
teach.note: Bukhari and Muslim (Abu Hurairah). Ask: what does the repetition teach? Be sensitive to different family situations: speak about 'those who raise you'.

teach.heading: Obedience and limits
teach.note: Qur'an 31:15: if they strive to make you associate with Me, do not obey, but accompany them in this world with kindness. Mention gently for older children's understanding.

teach.heading: Acts of kindness
teach.note: Make a family kindness chart. Share at least one achievable action. Praise sincere pledges.

practice: What is the dua for parents?
Who is most deserving of kindness?
independent: Write a thank-you letter to a parent or carer
List five ways to honour parents
Explain the hadith in your own words
exit: What does Allah say about parents?
lessons.homework: Do three kind acts for parents or carers this week and record them.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: dua card with transliteration. Stretch: explain 31:15.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Akhlaq and hadith: trust, family and neighbours
lessons.title: Neighbours, guests and kind speech
objectives: State the hadith on neighbours, guests and speech
Describe how to honour guests
Describe how to treat neighbours well

keywords.def: person who lives or sits close to you

starter: What do we say when we meet?

teach.heading: The hadith
bullets: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day
should speak good or be silent
teach.note: Bismillah. Bukhari and Muslim (Abu Hurairah). The Prophet ﷺ said these as signs of faith. Ask: how does faith show in daily life?

teach.heading: Neighbours
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said Jibril kept advising him about the neighbour until I thought he would make him an heir (Bukhari and Muslim, Aisha). Also: share your food (Muslim, Abu Dharr). Discuss how to be a good neighbour as a child.

teach.heading: Guests
teach.note: Welcome guests with a smile and salam. Teach manners as guest too: do not stay too long and be grateful. Role-play.

teach.heading: Kind speech
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said a good word is charity (Bukhari and Muslim). Revisit Year 2 hadith. Ask: what is the difference between speaking good and silence?

teach.heading: Community project
teach.note: Plan a small act for a neighbour, e.g. a card. Check safety rules and parental supervision.

practice: Name a manner of a good guest.
independent: Plan how to welcome a guest in your home
Write a note to a neighbour
Compare the two parts of the hadith
exit: Who deserves honour according to the hadith?
What does Jibril's advice about neighbours teach?
lessons.homework: Greet a neighbour with salam and do a small kindness (with an adult).
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario cards with images. Stretch: write a short speech on hospitality in Islam.

lessons.title: Bridge: Iman and the six articles
lessons.bigQuestion: Which of these would change how you act tomorrow: believing angels write your deeds, or believing in the Last Day?
objectives: To understand what Muslims believe in each of the six articles of iman
successCriteria: All: name the six articles in order
Most: say one thing we believe about each
Some: explain how one article changes how we act

keywords.def: beings made from light who obey Allah
people chosen by Allah to deliver His message
Allah's knowledge and plan for everything

hook.text: Which of these would change how you act tomorrow: believing angels write your deeds, or believing in the Last Day?
hook.a: Both. Iman is not only in the heart: it changes what we do.

islamicLink.text: Allah says the believers 'all believe in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers' (al-Baqarah 2:285).

starter.q: What did Jibril ask about first?
What is ihsan?
starter.a: Worshipping Allah as if you see Him
options: Worshipping Allah as if you see Him

starter.q: Name the five pillars of Islam.

teach.heading: The six articles
teach.note: Count on fingers. Allah mentions these together in al-Baqarah 2:285 and an-Nisa 4:136.

teach.heading: Angels and books
teach.note: Keep it brief: this is a bridge. Name the prophets: Musa, Dawud, Isa, Muhammad ﷺ.

teach.heading: Messengers, the Last Day, qadar
bullets: Allah knows and plans all; we still choose
teach.note: Muhammad ﷺ is the last messenger. On the Last Day each deed is weighed. Qadar: trust Allah and try your best.

check.q: Which article means Allah knows and plans everything?
check.why: Qadar is Allah's decree. Angels and books are other articles.

teach.heading: Iman in action
teach.note: Ask pupils to match each belief to an action.

cards: I try to do good every day
I stay calm when plans change

practice.q: Write one sentence about each of the six articles.
practice.a: For example: I believe Allah is One; angels obey Allah; ...
practice.model: I believe in Allah, the One. I believe angels are made of light and obey Him. I believe in His books, including the Qur'an.

practice.q: Which book came to Isa?
practice.a: The Injil

independent.q: Make a six-section 'iman wheel': each section names an article and gives one action it leads to.
independent.a: Six sections, each with an article and a matching action.
independent.model: Teacher fills the first section: Allah: I pray to Him alone.

independent.q: Extend: why do Muslims say in sha Allah?
independent.a: Because of belief in qadar: only Allah knows what will happen.

independent.q: Stretch: choose one article and explain how it helps a person who is sad.
independent.a: For example: qadar helps because Allah's plan is wise and He rewards patience.

exit.q: Which is NOT one of the six articles?
Back to our ponder: which belief will change how you act tomorrow, and how?
exit.a: For example: angels write my deeds, so I will speak kindly.

lessons.homework: Teach the six articles to someone at home using the iman wheel.
lessons.send: SEND: wheel template with pictures. EAL: sentence starter 'I believe in ...'. Stretch: link two articles together.
resources: Slides
Reliable children's seerah book (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Pupil PDF worksheet: iman wheel template
Colouring pencils

pictures.alt: A wheel with spokes, like the six articles
An old page of the Qur'an
A balance: deeds are weighed on the Last Day

lessons.title: Opposition and patience: Bilal and Sumayyah (رضي الله عنهما)
lessons.bigQuestion: What gives a person the strength to stay true to what they believe when others try to force them to give it up?
objectives: To understand how the early Muslims stayed patient and firm in their belief when they were treated cruelly
successCriteria: All: say who Bilal and Sumayyah were
Most: explain what 'Ahad, Ahad' showed about Bilal's belief
Some: explain how Abu Bakr helped and what this teaches about standing up for others
lessons.smsc: Moral: courage and standing up for what is right; Spiritual: firm iman

keywords.def: patience: staying firm when things are hard
treat people cruelly because of their beliefs
being brave to do what is right

hook.text: What gives a person the strength to stay true to what they believe when others try to force them to give it up?
hook.a: Strong iman and trust in Allah: Bilal kept saying 'Ahad, Ahad' (One, One).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'O you who believe, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient' (al-Baqarah 2:153).

starter.q: Bismillah. Where did the first revelation come?
Who was the first person to believe in the Prophet ﷺ?
What did the Prophet ﷺ call people to?

teach.heading: Why the Quraysh were angry
bullets: Islam said: worship Allah alone, not idols
It taught all people are equal before Allah
Some leaders feared losing power and trade
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Keep descriptions calm and age-appropriate.

teach.heading: Bilal: 'Ahad, Ahad'
bullets: Bilal was an enslaved man in Makkah
His master hurt him on the hot sand
He kept saying: Ahad, Ahad (One, One)
teach.note: The seerah reports this. Abu Bakr bought Bilal and freed him. Umar later said: 'Abu Bakr is our master, and he freed our master', meaning Bilal (Bukhari).

teach.heading: Sumayyah: the first martyr
bullets: Sumayyah and her family, the family of Yasir
She was the first Muslim to die for her faith
teach.note: The seerah reports the Prophet ﷺ encouraging the family of Yasir to be patient, with Paradise as their promise. Do not describe the harm in detail.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

options: Bilal believed Allah is One, whatever happened
check.why: Ahad means One: his tawheed stayed firm.

practice.q: Explain why Bilal kept saying 'Ahad, Ahad'.
practice.a: He believed Allah is One and would not say otherwise, even when he was hurt.
practice.model: Point: Bilal showed strong iman. Evidence: he kept saying 'Ahad, Ahad' on the hot sand. Explain: Ahad means One, so he held on to tawheed. Link: patience (sabr) for Allah.

practice.q: Who freed Bilal?
practice.a: Abu Bakr

practice.q: Who was the first martyr in Islam?
practice.a: Sumayyah

independent.q: Write a short diary-style page (no drawings of people) about courage in Makkah in the portal response box. Start: 'In Makkah, the early Muslims showed courage when ...'
independent.a: Mentions Bilal's 'Ahad', Sumayyah's firmness, Abu Bakr freeing Bilal, and patience.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first sentence: 'In Makkah, the early Muslims showed courage when they would not give up worshipping Allah alone.'

independent.q: Extend: how did Abu Bakr use his wealth for Allah?
independent.a: He bought and freed Muslims who were enslaved and mistreated, such as Bilal.

independent.q: Stretch: how can we stand up for someone treated unfairly today?
independent.a: Speak kindly, tell a trusted adult, support them, make du'a.

exit.q: 'Ahad' means ...
Back to our ponder: what gave Bilal his strength?
exit.a: His iman: belief that Allah is One, and patience.

lessons.homework: Find out one more fact about Bilal (he later became the first mu'adhdhin) and share it next lesson.
lessons.send: SEND: three picture-free story cards to order. EAL: diary sentence starters. Stretch: compare Bilal's patience with Nuh's.
resources: Slides
School-approved seerah text (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Pupil PDF worksheet: courage diary frame

lessons.title: The Hijrah to Abyssinia and the just king
lessons.bigQuestion: Would you leave your home to keep your faith safe? What would be hardest to leave?
objectives: To understand why some Muslims moved to Abyssinia and why its king protected them
successCriteria: All: find Makkah and Abyssinia on a map
Most: explain why the Muslims chose Abyssinia
Some: explain what Ja'far's speech and the king's answer show about justice
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: using a map of Africa and Asia across the Red Sea
lessons.smsc: Moral: justice and fairness; Cultural: Muslims and a Christian king living in peace

keywords.def: moving to another place for the sake of Allah
a kingdom in Africa, around modern Ethiopia
the title of the just king of Abyssinia

hook.text: Would you leave your home to keep your faith safe? What would be hardest to leave?
hook.a: The early Muslims did: they left family and homes for Allah and found safety with a just king.

islamicLink.text: Justice is loved by Allah: 'Indeed, Allah commands justice and good conduct' (an-Nahl 16:90).

starter.q: Bismillah. 'Ahad' means ...
Who freed Bilal?
Who was the first martyr in Islam?

teach.heading: A safe place
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ told some Muslims to go to Abyssinia
Its king was known to be just
They crossed the Red Sea, about 615 CE
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Show a map of Arabia, the Red Sea and Abyssinia.

teach.heading: The Quraysh follow
bullets: Two Quraysh envoys brought gifts to the king
They asked him to send the Muslims back
The king said: first I will hear them
teach.note: This is reported in the seerah (also by Ahmad). A just ruler listens to both sides.

teach.heading: Ja'far speaks
bullets: We used to worship idols and do wrong
Allah sent a messenger who taught truth
teach.note: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, the Prophet's ﷺ cousin. The king was moved by the recitation and protected the Muslims. When An-Najashi died, the Prophet ﷺ prayed the funeral prayer for him (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: Why did the king let the Muslims stay?
check.why: He heard both sides and judged fairly.

practice.q: Explain why the Muslims went to Abyssinia.
practice.a: They were being hurt in Makkah; the Prophet ﷺ sent them to a just king who would protect them.
practice.model: Point: they needed safety. Evidence: in Makkah they were persecuted, and Abyssinia had a just king. Explain: the Prophet ﷺ chose a place where they could worship in peace. Link: this was a hijrah for Allah.

practice.q: Which sea did they cross?
practice.a: The Red Sea

practice.q: Who spoke for the Muslims?
practice.a: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib

independent.q: On the pupil PDF map, mark Makkah, the Red Sea and Abyssinia, then write three sentences: why they left, what Ja'far said, what the king did.
independent.a: Correct map; three sentences on persecution, Ja'far's speech and the king's protection
independent.model: Teacher marks Makkah and writes sentence 1: 'The Muslims left because they were treated cruelly in Makkah.'

independent.q: Extend: what did the king do before deciding?
independent.a: He listened to both the envoys and the Muslims.

independent.q: Stretch: what makes a ruler just? Give two features.
independent.a: Listens to both sides; protects the weak; does not take bribes

exit.q: An-Najashi was a ...
Back to our ponder: what was hardest for those Muslims to leave, and why did they go?
exit.a: Family and home; to keep their faith safe.

lessons.homework: Tell someone at home about the just king and why listening to both sides is fair.
lessons.send: SEND: map with labels to drag. EAL: word bank (refuge, king, just). Stretch: explain why the Prophet ﷺ prayed for An-Najashi.
resources: Slides
School-approved seerah text (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Pupil PDF worksheet: map of Arabia, the Red Sea and Abyssinia
Atlas or online map

lessons.title: Umar ibn al-Khattab (رضي الله عنه) accepts Islam
lessons.bigQuestion: Can someone who was strongly against something become its biggest supporter? What could change them?
objectives: To understand how Umar came to Islam and why it gave the Muslims strength
successCriteria: All: retell how Umar became Muslim in order
Most: explain why the Qur'an changed Umar's heart
Some: explain how one person's change helped the whole community
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: the power of the Qur'an; Moral: never giving up on people

keywords.def: when someone's beliefs and feelings change

hook.text: Can someone who was strongly against something become its biggest supporter? What could change them?
hook.a: Yes: Umar opposed Islam, but hearing the Qur'an changed his heart.

islamicLink.text: Allah says the Qur'an is guidance and healing for the believers (Fussilat 41:44): its words can change a heart.

starter.q: Bismillah. Where did some Muslims go for safety?
Who spoke to the king for the Muslims?
Which surah did Ja'far recite?

teach.heading: Umar before Islam
bullets: Umar was strong and respected in Makkah
At first he was against Islam
He set out angry one day
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. This story is reported in the seerah.

teach.heading: The story in order
teach.note: Pupils hold up fingers for each step.

timeline.text: Umar hears his sister and her husband are Muslim
He finds them reading the Qur'an
He reads the start of Surah Ta Ha
His heart softens; he goes to the Prophet ﷺ

teach.heading: A strength for the Muslims
bullets: Muslims could now pray more openly
Ibn Mas'ud: 'We have been strong since Umar became Muslim'
teach.note: Ibn Mas'ud's words are in Bukhari.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

options: Hearing the words of the Qur'an

practice.q: Explain how Umar's Islam helped the Muslims.
practice.a: He was strong and respected, so the Muslims felt safer and could worship more openly.
practice.model: Point: Umar's Islam made the Muslims stronger. Evidence: Ibn Mas'ud said they had been strong since Umar became Muslim (Bukhari). Explain: people feared him, so the Muslims could pray more openly. Link: Allah guides whom He wills.

practice.q: Which surah did Umar read?
practice.a: Ta Ha

independent.q: Write the story as a five-box storyboard on the pupil PDF (words and objects only: a scroll, a door, a path).
independent.a: Five boxes in the right order with a sentence each
independent.model: Teacher fills box 1: a path leading away from a house: 'Umar set out angry.'

independent.q: Extend: what does Umar's story teach about not giving up on people?
independent.a: Anyone can be guided; we should be kind and make du'a for them.

independent.q: Stretch: why might the Qur'an's words have such power?
independent.a: They are Allah's words: true, beautiful and speaking to the heart.

exit.q: Before Islam, Umar was ...
Back to our ponder: what changed Umar?
exit.a: Hearing the Qur'an softened his heart.

lessons.homework: Read the first few ayat of Surah Ta Ha in translation with your family.
lessons.send: SEND: five ready-written story strips to order. EAL: storyboard captions to complete. Stretch: compare Umar's change with the people of Makkah's opposition.
resources: Slides
School-approved seerah text (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Pupil PDF worksheet: five-box storyboard
Mushaf or printed opening of Surah Ta Ha (translation of the meaning)

An old door

lessons.title: The boycott in the valley
lessons.bigQuestion: If no one would sell you food or talk to you for three years, how would you keep going?
objectives: To understand how the Prophet's ﷺ family and the Muslims stayed patient through the boycott
successCriteria: All: say what a boycott is
Most: describe how hard life was in the valley
Some: explain how the boycott ended and what it teaches about patience
lessons.smsc: Moral: injustice of punishing a group; Spiritual: patience and hope

keywords.def: refusing to buy, sell or meet with a group

hook.text: If no one would sell you food or talk to you for three years, how would you keep going?
hook.a: With patience, sharing and trust in Allah, as the Prophet's ﷺ family did.

islamicLink.text: Allah promises: 'For indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease' (ash-Sharh 94:5-6).

starter.q: Bismillah. Which surah did Umar read?
Where did the just king rule?
'Ahad' means ...

teach.heading: What was the boycott?
bullets: The Quraysh leaders wrote an agreement
No trading, marrying or friendship with Banu Hashim
It was hung in the Ka'bah
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. The seerah dates it to about three years (c. 616 to 619 CE).

teach.heading: Life in the valley
bullets: Very little food; children were hungry
A few kind people secretly sent food
teach.note: Keep it gentle. Ask: how do you think they kept their hope?

teach.heading: How it ended
bullets: Some Makkans felt it was unfair
The agreement was found eaten by insects
Only 'In Your name, O Allah' was left, as the seerah reports
teach.note: The seerah reports this. Use it to show Allah's help comes, and some people of conscience spoke up.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

options: Refusing to trade or meet with a group
check.why: A boycott cuts people off from trade and friendship.

practice.q: Describe two hardships of the boycott.
practice.a: Not enough food; no trade; cut off from friends and family
practice.model: Teacher: First hardship: there was very little food, so children were hungry. Second: no one would trade or speak with them, so they felt alone.

practice.q: Who was the boycott against?
practice.a: Banu Hashim, the Prophet's ﷺ clan
options: Banu Hashim, the Prophet's ﷺ clan

practice.q: About how long did it last?
practice.a: About three years

independent.q: In the portal response box, write a message of hope (from today, to the people in the valley). Start: 'Even though you are hungry and alone, ...'
independent.a: Mentions patience, trust in Allah, sharing, and that the hardship will end.
independent.model: Teacher writes: 'Even though you are hungry and alone, Allah sees your patience, and every hardship has an end.'

independent.q: Extend: why did some Makkans help secretly?
independent.a: They knew it was unfair and cared for their relatives.

independent.q: Stretch: link to 94:5-6 'With hardship comes ease'. What does it promise?
independent.a: Hardship does not last for ever; ease comes with it.

exit.q: What was left on the eaten agreement?
Back to our ponder: how did they keep going?
exit.a: Patience, sharing and trust in Allah.

lessons.homework: Learn 94:5-6 ('With hardship comes ease') in translation and tell a family member what it means.
lessons.send: SEND: hardship picture cards (empty bowl, closed shop). EAL: frame for the message of hope. Stretch: compare the boycott with the persecution of Bilal.
resources: Slides
School-approved seerah text (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Pupil PDF worksheet: message of hope frame
Mushaf or printed ash-Sharh 94:5-6 (translation of the meaning)

An empty bowl: hunger in the boycott

lessons.title: The Year of Sorrow
lessons.bigQuestion: Is it wrong to feel sad when something bad happens? What helps?
objectives: To understand how the Prophet ﷺ coped with losing Khadijah and Abu Talib and what we learn about grief and patience
successCriteria: All: name the two people the Prophet ﷺ lost
Most: explain why this year was so hard
Some: explain how Muslims can face sadness with patience and du'a
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: grief and patience; Moral: caring for others who are sad

keywords.def: the year the Prophet ﷺ lost Khadijah and Abu Talib

hook.text: Is it wrong to feel sad when something bad happens? What helps?
hook.a: No: the Prophet ﷺ felt sad too. Patience, du'a and family help.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And We will surely test you ... but give good news to the patient' (al-Baqarah 2:155).

starter.q: Bismillah. A boycott means ...
starter.a: Refusing to trade or meet with a group
options: Refusing to trade or meet with a group

starter.q: About how long did the boycott last?
What does 94:5 promise?

teach.heading: Two great losses
bullets: Abu Talib, his uncle who protected him
Khadijah, his wife who believed first
Both died in the same year, about 619 CE
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Speak gently; some pupils may have lost someone.

teach.heading: Why so hard?
teach.note: Pupils add ideas in the chat.

teach.heading: Sad but patient
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ wept but said only what pleases Allah
He kept going with his mission
teach.note: When his son Ibrahim died, the Prophet ﷺ wept and said the eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: Who protected the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah?
check.why: Abu Talib protected him, even though he did not accept Islam.

practice.q: Explain why the Year of Sorrow was so hard for the Prophet ﷺ.
practice.a: He lost his protector Abu Talib and his loving wife Khadijah, and the Quraysh harmed him more.
practice.model: Point: he lost two of the people closest to him. Evidence: Abu Talib protected him; Khadijah comforted and supported him. Explain: without Abu Talib, the Quraysh harmed him more. Link: he still stayed patient.

practice.q: Khadijah was the first to ...
practice.a: Believe in him

independent.q: Make a 'comfort card' on the pupil PDF: three things that help when we are sad (from today's lesson), each with an example.
independent.a: Patience; du'a; talking to family or a trusted adult; remembering Allah
independent.model: Teacher writes: 1) Du'a: tell Allah how you feel and ask for help.

independent.q: Extend: what did the Prophet ﷺ say when his son died?
independent.a: The eyes weep and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord.

independent.q: Stretch: why did the Prophet ﷺ keep loving Khadijah's memory?
independent.a: She believed in him first and supported him with her wealth and love.

exit.q: The Year of Sorrow was about ...
Back to our ponder: is it wrong to feel sad? What helps?
exit.a: No; patience, du'a and family help.

lessons.homework: Make du'a for someone you know who is going through a hard time.
lessons.send: SEND: feelings word bank; comfort card with pictures of a hand, a book, a home. EAL: frame 'When I am sad, I can ...'. Stretch: explain how sadness and sabr go together.

School-approved seerah text (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Pupil PDF worksheet: comfort card

Rain on a window: a calm, sad mood

lessons.title: The Night Journey and Ascent: the gift of salah
lessons.bigQuestion: After the hardest year of his life, what do you think Allah gave the Prophet ﷺ, and why?
objectives: To understand the Isra and Mi'raj and why salah was given as a special gift
successCriteria: All: say what the Isra and the Mi'raj were
Most: explain how fifty prayers became five
Some: explain why salah is called a gift
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: salah as a gift from Allah

keywords.def: the Night Journey from Makkah to Jerusalem

hook.text: After the hardest year of his life, what do you think Allah gave the Prophet ﷺ, and why?
hook.a: The Isra and Mi'raj: comfort, honour and the gift of salah.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Exalted is He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa' (al-Isra 17:1).

starter.q: Bismillah. Who did the Prophet ﷺ lose in the Year of Sorrow?
Where did the Muslims go for safety earlier?
What does sabr mean?

teach.heading: The Night Journey
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Read al-Isra 17:1 in translation. Al-Buraq is described in Bukhari and Muslim. No pictures of al-Buraq or prophets.

teach.heading: The Ascent
bullets: Allah gave the command of salah
teach.note: Bukhari and Muslim describe the Mi'raj.

teach.heading: Fifty become five
teach.note: Show the ratio idea: five prayers, the reward of fifty.

timeline.label: Reward
timeline.text: Five prayers with the reward of fifty

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.why: Al-Isra 17:1: from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa.

practice.q: Explain the difference between the Isra and the Mi'raj.
practice.a: Isra: the night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem. Mi'raj: the ascent through the heavens.
practice.model: Teacher: Isra is the journey across the earth: Makkah to Jerusalem. Mi'raj is the journey up: through the heavens, where salah was given.

practice.q: How many prayers were first commanded?
practice.a: Fifty

practice.q: Which surah begins with the Night Journey?
practice.a: Al-Isra (17)

independent.q: Make a two-part journey map on the pupil PDF: Makkah to Jerusalem (Isra), then upwards (Mi'raj), with one fact on each stage and a sentence: 'Salah is a gift because ...'
independent.a: Correct stages and facts; salah is a gift because it is our direct link with Allah, given in the heavens
independent.model: Teacher labels stage 1: Makkah to Jerusalem in one night: the Isra (17:1).
